sources.content: Spec GLM-41: per-tenant series limits in Glimmet. Glimmet stores metrics for many tenants in one shared cluster. Last quarter a single tenant added a request_id label to one metric and created 9 million new series in an hour, which pushed ingest latency past 30 seconds for every tenant. This spec adds a hard cap on active series per tenant, with a default of 500,000. A series counts as active if it received a sample in the last 2 hours. Caps are stored per tenant in the cluster's limits table.

When a tenant reaches its cap, Glimmet rejects samples for new series and keeps accepting samples for existing ones. The write API returns HTTP 429 with the header Glimmet-Limit: series. Operators change a tenant's cap with glimmetctl limits set. Rejected samples are counted in glimmet_rejected_samples_total with a reason label. Recording rules run inside Glimmet and are exempt from the limit. Rollout starts in staging on 3 February, then reaches production two weeks later.

claims.text: Glimmet's write API returns HTTP 429 when a tenant hits its series cap.
A Glimmet series counts as active if it received a sample in the last 2 hours.
Glimmet keeps accepting samples for existing series after a tenant reaches its cap.
Recording rules count toward a tenant's series limit in Glimmet.
The default Glimmet cap is 500,000 active series per tenant.
One tenant's request_id label created 9 million new Glimmet series in an hour.
